pending_commit.commit_message: kerberos: Add Kerberos configuration validator The Kerberos daemon should not accept all options in a Kerberos configuration, but only a whitelisted subset. Thus, this CL adds a class to validate configuration data. See https://web.mit.edu/kerberos/krb5-1.12/doc/admin/conf_files/krb5_conf.html for a description of the format and a list of all options. It was necessary to implement a parser for the configuration since that functionality is not publicly exposed by the MIT krb5 library. The parser is loosely based on prof_parse.c:parse_line(), see https://github.com/krb5/krb5/blob/master/src/util/profile/prof_parse.c#L277, but with a less C-like implementation and only checked array access for security. kerberos: Validate Kerberos configuration Hooks up the ConfigValidator class added in a previous CL to actually validate the configuration sent via SetConfig. Validation makes sure that the syntax is correct and that only whitelisted config options are used. If a user in Chrome adds a new Kerberos account, the account does not exist yet when the user modifies the config. In order to still allow Chrome to validate config, a new D-Bus method, ValidateConfig, is added that does not require an account. Since config is an untrusted user input, parsing is done in a jailed separate process. Moreover, the config is run through the actual krb5 parsing code to make sure it accepts it as well. CHROMIUM: add nl80211_sta_info enums Kernel support for following nl80211_sta_info enums is necessary for user-space to populate their respective entries 1. NL80211_STA_INFO_ACK_SIGNAL - support to get ack signal in probe client response and in station info from user 2. NL80211_STA_INFO_ACK_SIGNAL_AVG - avg signal strength of ACK frames 3. NL80211_STA_INFO_RX_MPDUS - total number of received packets 4. NL80211_STA_INFO_FCS_ERROR_COUNT - total number of packets (MPDUs) received with an FCS error 5. NL80211_STA_INFO_CONNECTED_TO_GATE - gate connectivity in station info 6. NL80211_STA_INFO_TX_DURATION - aggregate PPDU duration for all frames sent to the station 7. NL80211_STA_INFO_AIRTIME_WEIGHT - current airtime weight for station 8. NL80211_STA_INFO_AIRTIME_LINK_METRIC - airtime link metric for mesh station This CL is added as WAR to be in sync with linux-headers (chromium:1544980) without which collecting mesh link metric fails and this CL shall be reverted if and only if decided to pull the complete changes associated with each enums from upstream. arc: network: Recognize usb%d devices as ethernet When tethering to a Chrome OS device over usb, the network device shows up as usb%d which happen to be ignored by DeviceManager in arc-networkd. This prevents the multicast forwarder and the IPv6 provisioning code from being activated for such physical interfaces. This patch fixes adds "usb" as a possible name prefix for ethernet devices (as some other ethernet like configuration could appears with names like "usb%d") to solve the issue. Activating multicast forwarding and IPv6 for ARC when the upstream is cell is not expected to cause issues: IPv6 multicast forwarding: Not supported currently by arc-networkd. If it was, since pretty much all carriers assign full /64 unique prefixes to devices, the phone tethering routing will not forward the multicast packets to the upstream cellular networks. Only downstream tether clients of the phone could potentially receives packet from ARC or send multicast packets to ARC if the phone tethering routing would forward them. IPv4 multicast forwarding: The phone will only have a unique IPv4 address and is not expected to forward to the upstream cellular network multicast packets from any of its tether clients since necessarily a SNAT setup with a local IPv4 subnet for tether clients will be needed. IPv6 provisioning code: ARC will do SLAAC inside the /64 unique prefix assigned by the carrier which is expected to work. On IPv6 only cellular networks, Android phones already provision extra IPv6 addresses via SLAAC to implement 464 XLAT.
